claims.text: The target materials are high-entropy alloys in the near-solidus regime.
The target alloys have complex, multi-principal-element random solid-solution structures.
The proposed method combines replica-exchange molecular dynamics, tailored bias potentials, and a temperature ladder.
The simulations will be conducted near the melting point across representative HEA compositions spanning broad compositional space.
HEA melting can involve complex structural and chemical phase evolution.
Tailored bias potentials improve exploration of the free-energy landscape of HEA melting.
Bias potentials overcome sampling barriers associated with the HEA melting transition.
The enhanced-sampling method lowers effective free-energy barriers.
Lowering effective free-energy barriers enables rapid and statistically robust sampling of both solid and liquid states.
Robust sampling of solid and liquid states permits precise extraction of thermodynamic properties at melting.
The method can determine melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The method is more accurate than traditional approaches for determining these HEA thermodynamic properties.
The method improves computational throughput relative to conventional approaches.
Traditional DSC, dilatometry, standard CALPHAD, and first-principles methods have limited sensitivity or throughput in the complex HEA regime.
The approach is applicable across a broad range of HEA compositions, primarily near the solidus and up to moderate compositional complexity.
Extreme composition variations or exceptionally slow kinetics may prevent adequate phase-space sampling and limit performance.
Exact quantitative improvements cannot be specified without systematic experimental benchmarking across multiple HEA systems.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement, exemplified by at least 20% error reduction and/or comparable efficiency gains across at least three HEA compositions, would falsify the hypothesis.
